title: Legislative districts of Zamboanga del Sur
wikitext:
{{Short description|none}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Zamboanga del Sur''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Zamboanga del Sur]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Zamboanga}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Zamboanga del Sur were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935) and the historical [[Zamboanga (province)|Zamboanga Province]] (1935–1953). The enactment of Republic Act No. 711 on June 6, 1952 divided the old Zamboanga Province into [[Zamboanga del Norte]] and [[Zamboanga del Sur]] and provided them each with a congressional representative.{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 711 - An Act to Create the Provinces of Zamboanga del Norte and Zamboanga del Sur|author=Congress of the Philippines|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/8_republicacts.php?id=715|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=November 27, 2017|date=June 6, 1952}} Per Section 7 of Republic Act No. 711, the chartered cities of [[Zamboanga City|Zamboanga]] and [[Basilan]] formed part of Zamboanga del Sur's representation. The province, along with the two cities, first elected its representative starting in the [[1953 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1953 elections]]. Even after receiving its own city charter on June 21, 1969, [[Pagadian]] remained part of the representation of the Province of Zamboanga del Sur by virtue of Section 108 of Republic Act No. 5478.{{cite web|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/55_republicacts.php?id=5482|date=June 21, 1969|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=November 28, 2017|title=Republic Act No. 5478 – An Act Creating the City of Pagadian}} Zamboanga del Sur was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IX]] from 1978 to 1984. The province returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|three representatives, elected at-large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. [[Basilan]] (established as a province in 1973) and [[Zamboanga City]] (classified as a [[highly urbanized city]] in 1983) separately elected their representatives starting that year. Zamboanga del Sur was reapportioned into three [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional districts]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 27, 2017|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, and elected members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The passage of Republic Act No. 8973 and its subsequent ratification by plebiscite on February 22, 2001 separated Zamboanga del Sur's entire [[#3rd District (defunct)|third district]] to create the new province of [[Zamboanga Sibugay]].{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 8973 - An Act Creating the Province of Zamboanga Sibugay from the Province of Zamboanga del Sur and for Other Purposes|url=http://www.thecorpusjuris.com/legislative/republic-acts/ra-no-8973.php |author=Congress of the Philippines|date=November 7, 2000|website=The Corpus Juris|access-date=4 February 2017}} Per Section 7 of Republic Act No. 8973, Zamboanga del Sur's representation was reduced to two districts. The former third district first elected a representative under the designation ''[[Legislative districts of Zamboanga Sibugay#Lone District (defunct)|Lone congressional district of Zamboanga Sibugay]]'' beginning in the [[2001 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2001 election]]. The now-defunct [[#3rd District (defunct)|3rd district]] automatically became the representation of [[Zamboanga Sibugay]] upon its establishment in February 2001, but it was in May 2001 that this new province first elected [[Legislative districts of Zamboanga Sibugay#Lone District (defunct)|a representative under its own name]]. == Current districts == Zamboanga del Sur's current congressional delegation is composed of two members. {{Color box|{{party color|Lakas-Christian Muslim Democrats}}|border=darkgray}} [[Lakas–CMD]] (2) {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative districts and representatives of [[Zamboanga del Sur]] ! rowspan="2" |District ! colspan="3" |Current Representative ! rowspan="2" |Party ! rowspan="2" |Constituent [[Local government in the Philippines|LGUs]] ! rowspan="2" |Population (2020){{PH census|2020|01}} ! rowspan="2" |Area{{Cite web |title=List of Provinces |url=http://www.nscb.gov.ph/activestats/psgc/listprov.asp |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160419000512/http://www.nscb.gov.ph/activestats/psgc/listprov.asp |archive-date=April 19, 2016 |access-date=August 2, 2022 |website=PSGC Interactive |publisher=National Statistical Coordination Board}} ! rowspan="2" |Map |- ! colspan="2" |Image !Name |- ![[Zamboanga del Sur's 1st congressional district|1st]] | style="background:{{party color|Lakas-Christian Muslim Democrats}};" | | [[File:Rep.
